Beyond the Bell Curve

Can we see a currency crisis coming six months ahead? A research project across 110 emerging-market economies. Trained on 1990—2016 data, then applied to fresh data through 2023. Tip: hover the underlined termsLike this! Hover any dotted term for a definition..

What is this?
Imagine you wake up and your country's money suddenly buys only half as much as yesterday. Savings shrink, prices jump, imports get expensive. That's a currency crisisWhen a country's money rapidly loses a big chunk of its value against the US dollar..

This project asks: can we spot one coming about six months before it hits? The model watches two kinds of warning signs — ordinary cluesNormal signals: how much the currency has been slipping, and how bumpy it's been. (everyday economic signals) and extreme-move cluesSignals about rare, violent swings — the 'black swan' idea. (rare, violent swings — the "black swan" idea from Nassim Taleb).

The honest headlines: crises are genuinely hard to predict; the extreme-move clues give a small but reliable improvement; and, surprisingly, they carry most of the useful warning signal. This is a research tool, not a crystal ball — it estimates relative risk (who's more at-risk than whom), not exact odds.

1. Which warning signs matter most?

How to read this: longer bar = the model relies on that warning sign more. The red bars (extreme-move clues) do most of the work — the project's central finding.

2. Do the extreme-move clues actually help?

How to read this: each bar is one type of model. A positive bar means adding the extreme-move clues made it better at catching crises. (Hover a bar for the real model name and scores.)
What are these three models, and what's going on?
  • Simple model = Logistic Regression. A straight-line method: it finds the best simple relationship between the clues and crisis risk. Easy to understand, but can only see simple patterns.
  • Medium model = Random Forest. Builds hundreds of little decision trees and averages them, so it can catch more twisty, non-straight-line patterns.
  • Complex model = XGBoost. A powerful, state-of-the-art method that builds trees one after another, each fixing the last one's mistakes. Usually the strongest tool — when there's enough data.
The interesting twist: the extreme-move clues helped the simple model most (+33%) and the fancier models less (+7%). Why? The fancier models can partly figure out the extreme patterns on their own, so being handed them adds less. And strikingly, the complex model didn't win overall — because crises are so rare, even a powerful model can't find enough examples to learn from. That's a core lesson of this project: for rare, extreme events, a simple model plus the right extreme-move clues beats brute-force complexity. Fancier isn't automatically better.

3. Was that a fluke, or reliable?

How to read this: one bar per year. Red = the extreme-move clues helped that year. They helped in most years — so it's a real pattern, not luck.

4. Explore a country (through 2023)

Pick a country: you'll see a short note on its currency history (to check the model against reality), how at-risk it ranks now, and its risk over time.
Note: the model was trained only on 1990—2016 data. Values from 2017 onward are genuine predictions on fresh data — there's no official crisis list for those years to grade them, so they show who looks fragile, not verified accuracy.

Mini-glossary (plain English)

Currency crisisWhen a country's money rapidly loses a big chunk of its value against the US dollar (roughly a 30%+ drop).
Ordinary cluesNormal signals — how much the currency has slipped lately and how bumpy it's been.
Extreme-move cluesSignals about rare, violent swings: lopsidedness toward crashes, fat tails, counts of big sudden drops.
Risk rankingWhere a country sits versus the others, from most at-risk (#1) to least. The model is good at ordering risk.
Estimated risk (%)The model's honest guess of crisis chance. It stays low even for risky countries — because these events are genuinely rare.
Crisis windowThe months just before a real crisis — what the model tries to flag in advance (recorded up to 2016).

Built as an independent research project. The emphasis is honesty over hype — including reporting what the data cannot show.
